export const meta = {
  name: 'rfq-site-flows',
  description: 'Five investigators work the public challenge sites and Clef in parallel to find the shortest reliable flow for each part; a checker then tries to refute each site finding',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Investigate', detail: 'ERP group read, mailbox, specification portal, submission wizard, Clef measurement' },
    { title: 'Refute', detail: 'an independent checker repeats the decisive steps on the same site' },
  ],
}

const REPO = String.raw`C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\GitHub\The-Last-Team`
const S = String.raw`C:\Users\ADMINI~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-Administrator-Documents-GitHub-The-Last-Team\c8b91696-6cf4-42bb-80ed-10d1928a6515\scratchpad`

const COMMON = `
You are helping build a browser agent for a hackathon challenge ("From RFQ to bid"): a model-driven agent reads four German business websites (tender portal, supplier portal with a specification, an SAP-style ERP, a webmail), computes a bid and submits it. The agent's model sees each page as a TEXT SNAPSHOT with numbered controls and answers with actions. Every model call costs 5 to 15 seconds, so the number of model calls is what we must cut. Your job is an investigation on the REAL public practice websites, using the agent's own observation and action code through a command-line driver, playing the role of the model yourself.

HARD RULES
- Do not create, edit or delete any file inside the repository ${REPO}. You may read it. Write any scratch files only under ${S}\\wf (create your own subfolder there).
- Do not run git commands that change anything. Do not run the "atira" command line tool. Do not start any agent runs.
- Use only the browser tab assigned to you below (one site index). Other agents use the other tabs at the same time.
- Never request a signing code (TAN) and never submit a bid.
- Values you read on the websites may appear in your report to me, but your PROPOSED GUIDANCE text must be generic: it will go into a prompt that must also work on different websites, so it may not contain names, labels, addresses or identifiers of these websites.
- Report what you actually observed. If something did not work or you could not check it, say so plainly; a wrong "it works" costs us a 20-minute test run.

THE DRIVER (PowerShell)
  $env:PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8'; & "${REPO}\\my-agent\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe" "${S}\\tools\\drive.py" "${REPO}\\my-agent" SITE [options] [actions...]
SITE is 0 tender portal, 1 supplier/specification portal, 2 ERP, 3 webmail.
Options: --start (go to the site's entry address first) | --batch (run ALL given actions as ONE batch through the agent's batch executor, exactly as one model call would) | --max N (characters of the snapshot to print, default 6000) | --from N | --grep TEXT (print only snapshot lines containing TEXT, with two lines of context) | --shot FILE.jpg (save a screenshot; view it with your Read tool).
Actions, shorthand: login | click:ID | type:ID:TEXT | select:ID:OPTION | check:ID:true | goto:ADDRESS | press:KEY | expand:HEADING | scroll:down | back | look
Actions, full form: @FILE.json holding one action object or a list of them in the agent's own format, for example
  {"kind":"fill","fields":[{"id":8,"text":"x"},{"id":9,"text":"true"}],"submit_id":11}
  {"kind":"read_all","next_id":18,"reveal_ids":[9],"open_ids":[9,10],"follow_labels":["..."],"reveal_labels":["..."]}
Write such files with:  '...json...' | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 FILE.json   (JSON typed directly on the command line breaks on the quotes).
How it behaves:
- Each command reconnects to a persistent browser tab, so the page stays as it is between commands.
- Control ids are renumbered at every observation. Always take ids from the snapshot printed by your previous command.
- Without --batch each action runs after a fresh observation. With --batch the list runs as one batch: later actions are matched to the controls seen at batch start, and the batch stops at the first action that fails.
- "login" fills the login form with the practice credentials. Cookie banners, simple "temporarily unavailable" pages and informational notices with a close button are handled automatically before each observation.
- "goto" accepts only the site's entry address or an address that appeared as a link on the page just observed.
- The text printed after "--- snapshot" is exactly what the agent's model sees.
- If a command hangs for more than about 90 seconds, stop it. A stuck tab can be replaced: GET http://127.0.0.1:PORT/json/list, GET /json/close/TARGETID, then PUT /json/new?about:blank (ports: 9341 tender, 9342 specification, 9343 ERP, 9344 webmail). Then run the driver with --start.

THE read_all ACTION (the agent's tool for reading a lot in one call)
- next_id: the control that leads to the next page of a result set; every page is read until it is gone.
- reveal_ids: one example of each control that opens a hidden detail of a row or field; every control like it is opened on every page read, one at a time, and the text is taken after each.
- open_ids: links to open one after another (chosen results, or the tabs of one record); each is read.
- follow_labels (new, never yet run against the sites): visible names of views to open on each opened item, such as its tabs or linked views; a named view may lead to another named view.
- reveal_labels (new, never yet run against the sites): visible names of detail controls (buttons, not links) to open on every page read.
The code is in ${REPO}\\my-agent\\rfq\\browser\\actions.py (function read_all) and snapshot.py. Read it when the tool does something you do not expect, and report the defect with a concrete proposed fix. Do not edit it.

The task brief of the practice scenario (rules, tender reference VG-2027-7093, scenario date) is the "brief" field of ${S}\\scouting.json.
`

const INVESTIGATE_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string', description: 'What you found, in plain sentences, most important first' },
    minimal_sequence: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'The shortest reliable sequence of model calls for this part; one entry per model call, with the actions it holds' },
    evidence: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'For each claim: the command you ran and what it returned (counts, key lines), including what did NOT work' },
    harness_defects: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      what: { type: 'string' }, how_to_reproduce: { type: 'string' }, suggested_fix: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['what', 'how_to_reproduce'] } },
    proposed_generic_guidance: { type: 'string', description: 'Prompt wording for the agent that would make a model follow the minimal sequence; generic, no site-specific names' },
    not_verified: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'Anything you assumed or could not check' },
  },
  required: ['summary', 'minimal_sequence', 'evidence', 'harness_defects', 'proposed_generic_guidance', 'not_verified'],
}

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {

- Each command reconnects to a persistent browser tab, so the page stays as it is between commands.
- Control ids are renumbered at every observation. Always take ids from the snapshot printed by your previous command.

- next_id: the control that leads to the next page of a result set; every page is read until it is gone.
- reveal_ids: one example of each control that opens a hidden detail of a row or field; every control like it is opened on every page read, one at a time, and the text is taken after each.
- open_ids: links to open one after another (chosen results, or the tabs of one record); each is read.
- follow_labels (new, never yet run against the sites): visible names of views to open on each opened item, such as its tabs or linked views; a named view may lead to another named view.
- reveal_labels (new, never yet run against the sites): visible names of detail controls (buttons, not links) to open on every page read.

The task brief of the practice scenario (rules, tender reference VG-2027-7093, scenario date) is the "brief" field of ${S}\\scouting.json.

import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from urllib.parse import urlsplit


def origin(url: str) -> str:
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    return f"{parts.scheme}://{parts.netloc}"

    browser: object

    def install_handlers(self, page):
        page.set_default_timeout(7000)
        async def dialog_handler(dialog):
            self.dialogs.append(dialog.message)
            if self.confirm_final:

            else:

        page.on("dialog", dialog_handler)

60	def answer_from(ledger, context, settings, bus):
61	    """The best answer the evidence supports. A run without an answer scores nothing, so a calculation that
62	    fails still yields the decision and reference, with the failure listed as a gap."""
63	    try:
64	        return calculate(ledger, context, settings.surcharge_includes_setup, settings.rules_stage == "core")
65	    except Exception as error:
66	        bus.emit("calculation_failed", "rules", {"error": f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:300]}"})
67	        answer = {"tender_reference": context["reference"], "decision": "bid", "currency": "EUR",
68	                  "discount_percent": Decimal(0), "positions": [], "total_net": Decimal(0)}
69	        return Calculation(answer, gaps=[f"Calculation failed: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}"])

72	TASKS = {
73	    "tender": "Find the exact tender. First record TenderInfo and every TenderPosition from its bill of quantities, all in one call: the positions are needed by everyone else. Then record ALL clarification/Q&A entries, including withdrawals, amendments and commercial/packaging/delivery/setup/bonus keys. Page through the model-selected clarification result set. Open relevant tender documents when needed. Preserve dates, revision and requirement references. After facts, prepare registration/interest if required, but do not enter prices or sign. Tell others when all positions/Q&A are recorded.",
74	    "spec": "Find the technical specification for this tender, identify the revision explicitly marked current, and record SpecRevision with all requirements and catalogue groups, exact normalized attributes, pieces per set and usable/nominal stroke. Inspect superseded versions as candidates only when needed to establish revision status. Open the chosen ZIP/PDF/iframe documents. Share groups/requirements promptly so ERP can search. Do not calculate prices.",
75	    "erp": "Orient in the ERP and learn material/group searches. Watch shared evidence for specification catalogue groups and amended requirements. Search EACH required group precisely, inspect all candidates and record Material attributes/status, stock/lead times, carton size, surcharge and allocation masses, index/formula and ordinary setup fee. Record all dated PriceCondition entries/scales/currency/price units/FX keys for matching candidates. Record SearchCoverage only when every result in the selected group is inspected. Need_help for missing groups while continuing independent orientation; never use an empty broad catalogue crawl. Do not decide no_bid from missing evidence. Record evidenced zero fees/mass explicitly.",
76	    "mail": "Identify the logged-in bidder mailbox address/domain and record it in TenderInfo. Search by exact tender reference AND each relevant topic, checking inbox AND archive and all result pages. Record all candidate MailRecord approvals with sender/date/reference and structured payloads, including newer future or unrelated records so resolver can reject them. Collect discount approval, commercial clauses, technical reserve, packaging tariff, delivery commitment, FX fixing, setup pools, project bonus and metal index rates with validity windows. Read each full message; preserve raw clause text, do not calculate. Shared Q&A/spec/ERP may reveal keys or groups. Do not request a signing TAN yet."

80	async def orchestrate(run, settings, bus):
81	    shared = {}
82	    model = QwenClient(settings, bus)
83	    ledger = Ledger(bus)
84	    freeze_at, end_at = deadlines(run, settings)
85	    bus.emit("run_started", "orchestrator", {"budget_s": settings.run_budget_s, "model": settings.model_name})
86	    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
87	        context_task = asyncio.create_task(plan_context(model, run))
88	        sessions = await asyncio.gather(*(BrowserSession.connect(playwright, settings, site, i, run["access"])
89	                                         for i, site in enumerate(run["access"])))
90	        context = await context_task
91	        shared["runtime_context"] = context
92	        agents = {}
93	        for session in sessions:
94	            role = context["site_roles"].get(session.site["siteId"], "tender")
95	            agents[role] = BrowserAgent(role, session, model, bus, ledger, run, settings, shared)
96	        bus.emit("phase", "orchestrator", {"phase": "gather"})
97	        try:
98	            worker_tasks = dict(TASKS)
99	            if settings.rules_stage == "core":
100	                worker_tasks["mail"] = "Identify the logged-in bidder mailbox domain and record TenderInfo. First find the discount approvals for the exact tender reference in inbox and archive: record each candidate from its list row (sender, date, subject, reference), and open only the newest one from the authorized sender to read its percentage and any threshold. Then find revision-specific technical reserve approvals needed for usable stroke and FX fixing keys needed by ERP conditions. Record typed MailRecord payloads and preserve raw text. Prioritize these core inputs; other commercial adjustment topics are for a later phase. Search exact reference plus topic from observed evidence, never broad crawling. Do not request TAN yet."
101	                worker_tasks["erp"] += " Core phase priority: matching active materials, valid condition/scales, and stock/lead time. Record these promptly before investigating optional adjustments."
102	            initial_deadline = freeze_at - min(180, max(0, freeze_at - time.monotonic()) * 0.25)
103	            tasks = [asyncio.create_task(agent.run(worker_tasks.get(role, TASKS["tender"]), until=initial_deadline)) for role, agent in agents.items()]
104	            done, pending = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=max(0, initial_deadline - time.monotonic()))
105	            for task in pending:
106	                task.cancel()
107	            await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
108	            calc = answer_from(ledger, context, settings, bus)
109	            # Missing facts are routed by a runtime planner to any site, even if its role differs.
110	            for round_index in range(3):
111	                if calc.complete or time.monotonic() >= freeze_at - 20:
112	                    break
113	                bus.emit("phase", "orchestrator", {"phase": "followup", "gaps": calc.gaps})
114	                prompt = "Assign targeted follow-up investigations to site workers. Return JSON object mapping roles to task strings. Available roles: " + ", ".join(agents) + "\nGaps: " + json.dumps(calc.gaps) + "\nShared state: " + json.dumps(shared, default=str)
115	                try:
116	                    reply = await asyncio.wait_for(model.complete("planner", [{"role": "system", "content": "You coordinate missing evidence. Return only JSON. Route by observed affordances and task context; facts may live on any site."}, {"role": "user", "content": prompt}], max_tokens=1500), timeout=max(1, freeze_at - time.monotonic() - 10))
117	                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
118	                    break
119	                try:
120	                    assignments = json.loads((reply.content or "").removeprefix("```json").removesuffix("```").strip())
121	                except ValueError:
122	                    break
123	                followups = [asyncio.create_task(agents[role].run(task, max_steps=25, until=freeze_at)) for role, task in assignments.items() if role in agents]
124	                if followups:
125	                    _, unfinished = await asyncio.wait(followups, timeout=max(0, freeze_at - time.monotonic()))
126	                    for task in unfinished:
127	                        task.cancel()
128	                    await asyncio.gather(*followups, return_exceptions=True)
129	                calc = answer_from(ledger, context, settings, bus)
130	            for step in calc.trace:
131	                bus.emit("trace_step", "rules", step)
132	            answer = validate_answer(calc.answer, run["answer_schema"])
133	            bus.emit("answer_frozen", "orchestrator", {"answer": answer, "gaps": calc.gaps, "complete": calc.complete})
134	            if run["submission"]["kind"] != "site":
135	                from ..platform import submit_api_answer
136	                result = submit_api_answer(run, settings.run_token, answer)
137	            else:
138	                target = next(s for s in sessions if s.site["siteId"] == run["submission"]["siteId"])
139	                submitter = BrowserAgent("submitter", target, model, bus, ledger, run, settings, shared)
140	                mailbox = agents.get("mail")
141	                if mailbox is None:
142	                    raise ValueError("Runtime plan did not identify a mailbox worker")
143	                try:
144	                    result = await asyncio.wait_for(submit_frozen(submitter, mailbox, answer, context, end_at), timeout=max(1, end_at - time.monotonic()))
145	                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
146	                    result = {"submitted": False, "reason": "submission deadline reached"}
147	            bus.emit("run_finished", "orchestrator", {"result": result, "cost": model.total_cost})
148	            return result
149	        finally:
150	            await asyncio.gather(*(s.close() for s in sessions))

Decision, reference and the 5 % discount are right; the total is wrong. Every lost point traces back to the base price on four positions. That is the number-format trap I found tonight: the ERP writes some prices in US format and some in German, with a tag per value. Their number parser is close to mine but mangles those four; fixing it is plausibly worth around 20 points, though I haven't confirmed the exact cause in their code.

## What we know

**Scoring (from real breakdowns)**
- Decision, reference, discount, total and consistency are 5 points each; two extra checks (the withdrawn Q&A quantity and the metal index) are 5 each.
- Each position is 13 points: material 2.6, quantity 1.95, base price 1.95, and 1.3 each for surcharge, packaging, bonus, unit price and lead time.
- An empty signed bid scores 10.

**The public sites**
- Every site puts several dependent steps in front of each page: unlock sliders, receipt-number forms, popups whose prominent button leads away.
- Lists are paged in ones or threes, with details hidden per row.
- Look-alikes exist everywhere: a blocked material identical to the right one, an approval for a near-identical reference, superseded revisions.
- Numbers carry a format tag, and dates use mixed formats.
- The sites run on a January 2027 clock.
- The public scouting login is shared by all teams, so signing there can fail because someone else requested a code.

**The platform**
- About one model call in eight gets no response in the sandbox; healthy calls start answering in about 1.3 seconds.
- Qwen allows 32 calls at once per team, shared with teammates' runs.
- The platform keeps only the last 12 minutes or so of a run's log.

**Our agent (`claude-build`, 20 local commits, nothing pushed)**
- **Verified on the platform:** it completes, signs and is eligible (quality 10, 16:40, $0.20).
- **Verified by replaying real evidence:** it picks the right material and quantity, and the right base price and discount, for position 01.01.
- **Not good enough:** in 12 minutes of gathering it never collects enough to price more than one position. Each run costs about $0.20 to $0.25.
- **Known gap:** it would get 01.01's lead time and unit price wrong, because surcharge, packaging and the delivery commitment aren't applied in the stage we run.
- **Reasoning off:** one full local run recorded spec values that were not on the page and ended in a wrong no-bid. That one is not a server error; I compared the records with the page text. I've left reasoning on.
- **Untested in a run:** handing free workers new tasks, reading a record's sub-views by label, and the new number parser on live data.

**Still running:** the teammates' workflow you asked for (the wizard investigator has reported; four others are still working) and one local gather-only run. I'll let them finish and report, and start nothing new.

## Plan, for your decision

1. **Recommended first: fix the price parsing in the 78.1 agent.** I have its package downloaded and can prepare a patch locally for you or your teammate to apply. This is the shortest path to a much higher team score.
2. **Do not submit from our branch** unless a test run of it beats 78.1.
3. **If you want our agent continued in parallel:** finish gathering speed (the investigators' findings feed this), then switch on the full pricing rules and check them against the known-correct fields above, then submission with real positions.
4. **Clef:** wait for the measurement before deciding.

## Questions

1. Did you know about the 78.1 submission and the teammate's test runs? Which do you want: option 1, option 3, or both?
2. Is it acceptable to keep reasoning on for the workers that record evidence?
3. What did you mean by "jev"?
4. Can you re-export the PDF without a password, or send the password?
5. One fair-play judgement: I added a way for the model to name, by their visible labels, the tabs to open on each result (for example every material's price tab). The helper opens only what the model names. I believe that is within the rules, but it is the closest thing we have to the "crawler" line. Are you comfortable with it?

class Calculation(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_numbers_and_allocation(self):
        self.assertEqual(number("12.345,6 (de-DE)"), Decimal("12345.6"))
        self.assertEqual(number("412,750 (en-US)"), Decimal("412750"))
        self.assertEqual(number("1,5"), Decimal("1.5"))
        self.assertEqual(allocate(Decimal("1.00"), [Decimal(1)] * 3, ["b", "a", "c"], "largest_remainder"),
                         [Decimal("0.33"), Decimal("0.34"), Decimal("0.33")])

    def test_rules_end_to_end(self):
        evidence, problems = scenario()
        self.assertEqual(problems, [])
        result = calculate_bid(evidence)
        self.assertEqual(result["gaps"], [])
        answer = result["answer"]
        by = {p["position"]: p for p in answer["positions"]}
        # Quantities: withdrawal and future answers ignored; sets converted.
        self.assertEqual((by["2.1"]["quantity"], by["2.2"]["quantity"], by["2.3"]["quantity"]), (12, 12, 7))
        # Stroke 210 (amendment) + 2 x 5 reserve = 220 -> M-A; the inactive look-alike is ignored.
        self.assertEqual((by["2.1"]["material_number"], by["2.2"]["material_number"]), ("M-A", "M-B"))
        base_a = R(Decimal("11000") / 100 * Decimal("0.9"))  # 99.00
        base_b = R(Decimal("250.555"))
        self.assertEqual(Decimal(str(by["2.1"]["base_unit_price"])), base_a)
        self.assertEqual(Decimal(str(by["2.2"]["base_unit_price"])), base_b)
        # Discount: latest exact-reference approval no later than the scenario date, threshold met.
        undiscounted = R(12 * base_a + 12 * base_b + 7 * R(Decimal("12345.6") / 100 * Decimal("0.9")))
        self.assertGreaterEqual(undiscounted, Decimal("1000"))
        self.assertEqual(answer["discount_percent"], 4.0)
        d = Decimal("0.96")
        mass = Decimal("1.5") * Decimal("4.20")
        weights = [12 * 500, 12 * 700]
        pool = allocate(Decimal("100"), [Decimal(w) for w in weights], ["2.1", "2.2"], "largest_remainder")
        goods = [12 * base_a, 12 * base_b]
        credit = R((sum(goods) - 1000) * Decimal("0.02"))
        bonus = allocate(credit, goods, ["2.1", "2.2"], "largest_remainder")
        pack_a = math.ceil(12 / 4) * Decimal("2.50")
        final_a = R(base_a * d + mass * d + (Decimal(30) + pool[0] + pack_a - bonus[0]) / 12)
        self.assertEqual(Decimal(str(by["2.1"]["unit_price"])), final_a)
        self.assertEqual(Decimal(str(by["2.1"]["surcharge_per_unit"])), R(mass + (30 + pool[0]) / 12))
        self.assertEqual(Decimal(str(by["2.1"]["rebate_total"])), bonus[0])
        pack_b = math.ceil(12 / 5) * Decimal("2.50")
        final_b = R(base_b * d + (pool[1] + pack_b - bonus[1]) / 12)
        self.assertEqual(Decimal(str(by["2.2"]["unit_price"])), final_b)
        self.assertEqual(by["2.3"]["rebate_total"], 0.0)
        # Delivery: pooled M-A demand 19 <= stock 18? no -> 2.1 commitment (<=20) 4 weeks, 2.3 (ceiling 15) production.
        self.assertEqual((by["2.1"]["lead_time_weeks"], by["2.3"]["lead_time_weeks"], by["2.2"]["lead_time_weeks"]),
                         (4, 9, 1))
        total = sum(Decimal(p["quantity"]) * Decimal(str(p["unit_price"])) for p in answer["positions"])
        self.assertEqual(Decimal(str(answer["total_net"])), R(total))

    def test_failed_threshold_gives_zero_discount_and_missing_evidence_is_a_gap(self):

# Claude Code working notes

@AGENTS.md

The build plan is CODEX_BUILD_PROMPT.md (written for Codex, now executed by
Claude Code). Interfaces are in ARCHITECTURE.md, status in PROGRESS.md.

## Overrides from the human (2026-10-10) — these win over AGENTS.md and the brief

- Work on the local branch `claude-build`. Leave `main` untouched. Never push,
  fetch, pull or otherwise touch a remote. Commit locally after each working
  step; update PROGRESS.md after each milestone.
- Models: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next plus Clef only (hosted, free). There is no OpenAI
  access and no `OPENAI_API_KEY` team secret. The frontier escalation path and
  brief checkpoints 2, 3 and 6 are dropped. Keep the model router
  provider-agnostic (one interface, config-selected model) so another model
  with a proxy key could be plugged in later without code changes.
- Where the brief says "escalate to frontier": re-prompt Qwen with the
  validation error and a focused excerpt, at most two retries, then mark the
  field unknown and leave it blank. Never guess.
- Remaining checkpoints (stop and ask): before every scored submission; a rule
  ambiguity unresolved after two A/B runs; any fair-play doubt.
- Ask the human directly whenever something is ambiguous.
- Working system first (human, 2026-10-10): until a sandbox run scores, do not
  spend time or tokens on holdout gates, generality evaluations or new unit-test
  suites. Sandbox test runs against the real sites are the test loop. Keep the
  existing quick suite green and add tests only where they directly unblock a
  fix. The generality gates in AGENTS.md resume once a run is eligible.
- Keep it simple and light (human, 2026-10-10, said twice): few tests, few
  safeguards, no checking of everything. A safeguard added that day (replacing
  a "stuck" tab) misfired and trapped a worker in a loop, which is the cost of
  piling them on. Prefer one small, smart mechanism over several defensive
  layers, and verify on live runs. Elegance of the system is judged.

## Roles

The main session is Astra: plan, interfaces, resolver, rules engine, agent
loop, prompts, guards, submitter, watchdog, test-run diagnosis, review of every
Luna diff, commits and checkpoints. Well-specified implementation tasks go to
the `luna` subagent (.claude/agents/luna.md), one task at a time, each with
goal, files to touch, interface, acceptance check and files not to touch.
Luna never commits and never starts runs.

## Current milestone

M2 — thin end-to-end. M0 and M1 are done. Gate: the first sandbox test run
that is eligible (right reference, bid/no_bid decision, all positions,
quantities, consistent total). Earlier sandbox runs ended without an answer,
so signing and submission inside the deadline is the open problem. Reach this
gate before any polish, then M3 to M6 in order.

## Commands (run from the repository root)

Use the package interpreter. On Linux replace the path with
`my-agent/.venv/bin/python`.

```powershell
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests   # all synthetic tests
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest tests.rules.test_engine -v   # one module
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/fairplay_check.py        # before every package
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/package.py               # fairplay + tarball outside the checkout
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/run_local.py --dry       # parsed run and brief, redacted
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/run_local.py --orient    # log in and summarise each site
```

Sandbox test run (authorised, at most four at once): run the fair-play check,
then use the atira MCP tools `test_run`, `wait_for_run`, `diagnose_run`,
`run_logs` and `run_screenshot`, or `atira test-run .\my-agent --challenge rfq`.
Never call `atira submit` or the MCP submit tool without explicit approval.

The Atira CLI may be missing from PATH in a long-lived shell; it lives at
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira\bin\atira.cmd`. Run artifacts go to the external data
directory (`RFQ_DATA_DIR`, default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira-rfq\runs`), never into
the checkout.

# Working agreement

Read CODEX_BUILD_PROMPT.md before building. Astra owns architecture, interfaces,
resolver, rules, prompts, orchestration, snapshots, guards, submission, diagnosis,
milestone commits and human checkpoints. Luna implements one precise delegated
task at a time and returns its diff and checks to Astra; no unreviewed commits.

Only my-agent/ ships. Retain and extend the supplied starter. Python 3.12, uv,
Pydantic v2, Playwright CDP, Decimal and ROUND_HALF_UP are fixed choices.
Scripts must work on native Windows and Linux; use Python for packaging.

## Fair play and data

- A runtime model chooses navigation, searches and relevant documents. Helpers
  may extract a chosen page/document/result set, calculate, validate, retry,
  renew a session and fill forms. No fixed site paths, autonomous evidence
  crawlers or model-only-as-fallback implementations.
- Never persist values observed on public websites anywhere in this repository,
  including ignored files: references, material identifiers, prices, TANs,
  credentials, hostnames, labels, selectors or URLs. Runtime data comes from
  environment, the current run, its brief and observations. Tests are synthetic.
- Store every local run artifact outside the checkout in the configured data
  directory (default under the operating system temporary directory).
- Network access during a run is limited to the platform, model proxy and the
  run's websites. No local models; at most four supplied browsers, using CDP.
- Secrets are environment/team secrets and never enter source or telemetry.
- Never start a scored submission without explicit human approval. Sandbox test
  runs are authorized, with at most four concurrent team tests.
- Run scripts/fairplay_check.py before every package. Only my-agent/ is tarred.
- Frontier stays disabled and FRONTIER_MODEL unset pending human approval.

## Checkpoints

Stop and notify the human before any scored submission; choosing a frontier
model; shipping frontier enabled; unresolved rule ambiguity after two A/B
runs; any fair-play doubt; or half the development frontier budget spent.
After each completed milestone write five lines to PROGRESS.md and commit on
main. Reach the first eligible sandbox test before dashboard polish.

## Generality acceptance

Treat public challenge runs as development data. Never copy their values into
fixtures. Before a holdout evaluation, freeze the package, prompts, model and
configuration hashes; generate fresh synthetic seeds only after freezing.
Store seeds, expected answers, observations and results outside the checkout.
Use independent expected values and varied layouts, labels and information
placement. Exercise the actual model/browser loop, not scripted navigation.
Every used holdout seed is retired. A failure may become a development
regression, but changes must be evaluated on fresh seeds. Do not tune against
a reused holdout or claim that synthetic success guarantees private success.
Gate releases on fairplay plus the documented generality checks; report

# Claude Code working notes

@AGENTS.md

The build plan is CODEX_BUILD_PROMPT.md (written for Codex, now executed by
Claude Code). Interfaces are in ARCHITECTURE.md, status in PROGRESS.md.

## Overrides from the human (2026-10-10) — these win over AGENTS.md and the brief

- Work on the local branch `claude-build`. Leave `main` untouched. Never push,
  fetch, pull or otherwise touch a remote. Commit locally after each working
  step; update PROGRESS.md after each milestone.
- Models: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next plus Clef only (hosted, free). There is no OpenAI
  access and no `OPENAI_API_KEY` team secret. The frontier escalation path and
  brief checkpoints 2, 3 and 6 are dropped. Keep the model router
  provider-agnostic (one interface, config-selected model) so another model
  with a proxy key could be plugged in later without code changes.
- Where the brief says "escalate to frontier": re-prompt Qwen with the
  validation error and a focused excerpt, at most two retries, then mark the
  field unknown and leave it blank. Never guess.
- Remaining checkpoints (stop and ask): before every scored submission; a rule
  ambiguity unresolved after two A/B runs; any fair-play doubt.
- Ask the human directly whenever something is ambiguous.
- Working system first (human, 2026-10-10): until a sandbox run scores, do not
  spend time or tokens on holdout gates, generality evaluations or new unit-test
  suites. Sandbox test runs against the real sites are the test loop. Keep the
  existing quick suite green and add tests only where they directly unblock a
  fix. The generality gates in AGENTS.md resume once a run is eligible.
- Keep it simple and light (human, 2026-10-10, said twice): few tests, few
  safeguards, no checking of everything. A safeguard added that day (replacing
  a "stuck" tab) misfired and trapped a worker in a loop, which is the cost of
  piling them on. Prefer one small, smart mechanism over several defensive
  layers, and verify on live runs. Elegance of the system is judged.

- No runs until the human says so (2026-10-11): no sandbox test runs and no local
  agent runs, because the platform is being upgraded and results would mislead.
  Reading code, logs and scores, and offline tests, are fine.
- Nothing is submitted from `claude-build`. The team's latest passing submission
  (78.1, from a teammate's code line) is what goes into the final run.
- Fair play (human, 2026-10-11): get the best results first, then revisit the
  helper that opens views the model names by label before any submission.

## The team's 78.1 agent

A teammate's agent scores 78.1. Its whole loss is four base prices, caused by
its number parser joining every digit of a value that carries a note. The fix
is on the local branch `claude-patch-78`, checked out as a separate working
copy next to this one (`../The-Last-Team-78`): one commit importing the scored
package, one commit with the fix and two tests. It has not been test-run.

## Roles

The main session is Astra: plan, interfaces, resolver, rules engine, agent
loop, prompts, guards, submitter, watchdog, test-run diagnosis, review of every
Luna diff, commits and checkpoints. Well-specified implementation tasks go to
the `luna` subagent (.claude/agents/luna.md), one task at a time, each with
goal, files to touch, interface, acceptance check and files not to touch.
Luna never commits and never starts runs.

## Current milestone

M2 — thin end-to-end. M0 and M1 are done. Gate: the first sandbox test run
that is eligible (right reference, bid/no_bid decision, all positions,
quantities, consistent total). Earlier sandbox runs ended without an answer,
so signing and submission inside the deadline is the open problem. Reach this
gate before any polish, then M3 to M6 in order.

## Commands (run from the repository root)

Use the package interpreter. On Linux replace the path with
`my-agent/.venv/bin/python`.

```powershell
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests   # all synthetic tests
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest tests.rules.test_engine -v   # one module
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/fairplay_check.py        # before every package
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/package.py               # fairplay + tarball outside the checkout
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/run_local.py --dry       # parsed run and brief, redacted
.\my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/run_local.py --orient    # log in and summarise each site
```

Sandbox test run (authorised, at most four at once): run the fair-play check,
then use the atira MCP tools `test_run`, `wait_for_run`, `diagnose_run`,
`run_logs` and `run_screenshot`, or `atira test-run .\my-agent --challenge rfq`.
Never call `atira submit` or the MCP submit tool without explicit approval.

The Atira CLI may be missing from PATH in a long-lived shell; it lives at
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira\bin\atira.cmd`. Run artifacts go to the external data
directory (`RFQ_DATA_DIR`, default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira-rfq\runs`), never into
the checkout.

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.
</system-reminder>

Do not repeat what you already said in your final message; if the tool calls since your last text message did not change what you said, a brief closing note is enough. Still end each turn with a text message, even a short one, rather than ending on a tool call. If you are running as a subagent, ignore this section. Only your final message is returned to your caller, so put everything it needs there.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes.
